1. (Currently amended) A method for controlling a flow of air, the method comprising: establishing a level of vacuum in a booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device using a pump; determining whether the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value; and __terminating the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached the predetermined value, wherein the terminating step reduces a parasitic load on an engine driving the pump__.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein said terminating the flow of air is accomplished via a directional control valve __in response to a control signal generated based on the determination that the level of vacuum has reached the predetermined value__, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein said terminating the flow of air includes __simultaneously__ changing the direction of the flow of air and closing a flow path between the pump and the booster device.

4. (Previously presented) The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump.

5. (Previously presented) The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a path for a flow of air between the pump and the atmosphere.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 5, further comprising filtering the flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump via a filter __positioned to remove particulates before air enters the pump__.

7. (Previously presented) The method of claim 1, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system.

8. (Currently amended) A system for controlling a flow of air, the system comprising: a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; __a control module configured to determine when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value and generate a control signal__; and a directional control valve adapted to __receive the control signal and__ terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced __and parasitic load on an engine driving the pump is reduced__.

9. (Currently amended) The system of claim 8, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to __simultaneously__ change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device.

10. (Previously presented) The system of claim 9, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump.

11. (Previously presented) The system of claim 9, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere.

12. (Currently amended) The system of claim 11, further comprising a filter adapted for filtering a flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump __to remove particulates before air enters the pump__.

13. (Previously presented) The system of claim 8, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system.

14. (Currently amended) A motor vehicle comprising: an internal combustion engine; a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; and a system for controlling a flow of air from the booster device, the system including: __a control module configured to determine when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value and generate a control signal;__ a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; and a directional control valve adapted to __receive the control signal and__ terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value, such that a pressure differential across the pump and a parasitic load on the engine are reduced.

15. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 14, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to __simultaneously__ change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device.

16. (Previously presented) The vehicle of claim 15, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump.

17. (Previously presented) The vehicle of claim 15, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere.

18. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 17, further comprising a filter adapted for filtering the flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump __to remove particulates before air enters the pump__.

19. (Previously presented) The vehicle of claim 14, further comprising a braking system, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for the braking system.

20. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 14, wherein the engine is a compression-ignition type __diesel engine configured to drive the pump at variable speeds based on vacuum level in the booster device__.
